messages:
ben (SDK): Anyone else hit failures running the Node quickstart for embeddings? Getting a 400 that mentions an unknown field. Quick repro below.

ben (SDK): curl to REST works:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-v1","input":["test"]}'
```

ben (SDK): but the quickstart Node example uses SDK shape: 
```js
await client.embeddings.create({ modelName: 'embed-lite-v1', input: ['test'] })
```

ben (SDK): That generates body {"modelName":...} and server returns: 400 unknown parameter: modelName

neha (DevEx): Ugh. We recently changed examples to prefer modelName in SDK snippets to be more explicit. Looks like the runtime didn't get the mapping change.

kai (Infra): Confirmed in logs: runtime payload validation only validates for 'model'. No aliasing for 'modelName'. We intentionally left validation strict for safety after the schema migration.

ben (SDK): Two things here IMHO: SDK should do a compatibility shim (server mapping isn't guaranteed), and quickstart shouldn't diverge from what the server accepts.

ashley (PM): Meta: we've had three onboarding complaints about this in the past 48 hours. Can we fix the UX quickly and follow up with a longer migration plan?

ben (SDK): I'll push a fast client-side transform that renames modelName -> model before sending, add a test that asserts outgoing JSON, and cut a patch release.

kai (Infra): On the infra side I'm willing to add a permissive alias to the ingestion layer for a couple weeks, but I want us to log occurrences so we can monitor who still uses the old/new name.

neha (DevEx): I'll update the quickstart repo and docs to show the server-compatible example (use model) and add a short troubleshooting section noting the mismatch and which SDK versions have the change.

ben (SDK): Also noticed a subtle auth/retry difference: the SDK auto-refresh path will retry requests after a token rotation, but our sample app orchestrates refresh externally and can cause a race where the first request after a refresh gets a 401. That made the issue noisy in some CI runs.

kai (Infra): We log refresh events. If you can produce a deterministic test that forces refresh mid-call we can use it in CI. Otherwise add an integration test in client that simulates expired token + concurrent requests.

ben (SDK): Adding an integration that forces token expiry and fires 5 concurrent embedding requests to verify we don't leak 401s.

deploy-bot: ben/embeddings-param-fix pipeline started (#512) :hammer_and_wrench:

neha (DevEx): Action list:
- ben: client shim + unit/integration tests + patch release
- kai: alias on runtime + telemetry for alias usage
- neha: docs & quickstart update + troubleshooting note
- ashley: track customer tickets and email banners if needed

ben (SDK): ETA for patch + tests: end of day. Will ping when CI green.

neha (DevEx): Thanks. I'll hold a docs PR until the patch lands so quickstart refs don't flip back and forth. :white_check_mark:
